articles.title: The layer list
articles.summary: The layer list in the right column lists every layer of your paint. Use it to show, hide, lock, reorder and adjust layers.
articles.what: Open the layer list (right column) at the top of the right column (next to FINISHES). Each layer has a row with an eye, a lock, a thumbnail and a name. Click a name to select that layer and a card of buttons opens under it. + Layer adds a blank transparent layer; to bring in a picture, a logo or a sponsor, use Actions > Place image.... The Actions menu holds the bigger jobs: Place image..., blank layer, merge visible, flatten, Photoshop round trip and thumbnail size.
when: You opened a layered template and need to see what is in it.
You added a logo or sponsor and want to move, fade or hide it.
You want to hide the template guide layers to see your artwork alone.
how: Click the layer list at the top of the right column.
Click the eye on a row to hide or show that layer. Alt+click the eye to see only that layer.
Click a layer name to select it. Its button card and sliders appear under the row.
Type in the filter box to find a layer in a long list.
Click Done on the card to deselect the layer. Esc does not deselect it.

Ctrl+click names to pick several layers, then use the Merge button that shows the count.
Dragging a file onto the canvas replaces the paint. Use Actions > Place image... to add art on top instead.
pitfalls: A locked layer cannot be painted or changed. The AI copilot cannot edit it either, so unlock it first.
Hidden layers still exist. Hidden layers do not show in the render.

deep.heading: What each row shows
deep.body: Every layer row has an eye to show or hide it, a lock, a thumbnail and the name. Layers that belong to a Photoshop group sit under a group header. Click the header to collapse or expand the group, or click the eye on the header to show or hide the whole group at once. A small yellow tag on a row means one or more zones are restricted to that layer, which is handy when a finish suddenly stops showing.

deep.heading: Eye, solo and lock
deep.body: A plain click on the eye hides or shows that layer. Alt+click on the eye solos the layer so everything else disappears, and another click on the same eye restores the rest. The lock stops painting, moving and AI edits on that layer. Hidden layers stay in the file but are left out of the render.

deep.heading: Filter and thumbnails
deep.body: The filter box matches both the layer name and its group name, and a filtered list shows matches even inside collapsed groups. Actions includes a thumbnail size button that cycles through three sizes: small 24 pixels, medium 40 pixels and large 64 pixels. The choice is remembered between sessions.

deep.heading: Selecting and bulk work
deep.body: Click a name to select a layer and open its card of buttons. Ctrl+click names to pick several layers, then use the Merge button that shows the count. The Actions menu holds the document-wide jobs: Place image..., blank layer, flatten, merge visible, the Photoshop round trip and thumbnail size. The small note in the menu reminds you that Ctrl+click moves a layer and a double-click opens its effects.

faq.q: Why can I not paint on a layer?
faq.a: It is locked, hidden or a template guide. Unlock it by clicking the lock, and select the real artwork layer.

faq.q: What does the yellow tag on a layer mean?
faq.a: One or more zones are restricted to that layer. If the layer is hidden, those zones paint nothing.

faq.q: How do I see only one layer?
faq.a: Alt+click its eye, or use SOLO on its card. Click again to bring everything back.

faq.q: Do hidden layers go into the render?
faq.a: No. Hidden layers are left out. The guide layers (Wire, Mask, Car Mandatory) are left out of the render too, even when they are visible.

faq.q: I dropped a file on the canvas and lost my paint.
faq.a: Dropping replaces the source paint. Use Actions > Place image... to add art on top instead.

faq.q: Can the AI copilot change a locked layer?
faq.a: No. Unlock it first. The AI can change visibility, opacity and blend mode, but never delete, merge, rename or reorder layers.

faq.q: Plus layer does not ask for a file any more. How do I import a logo?
faq.a: Open Actions in the layer list and choose Place image.... + Layer now adds a blank layer.

faq.q: What does the + Layer button do now?
faq.a: It adds a blank transparent layer. To bring in a picture, a logo or a sponsor use Actions > Place image....

mistakes.symptom: A zone paints nothing
mistakes.cause: It is restricted to a layer that is hidden or gone.
mistakes.fix: Show the layer, or open the zone and clear its layer restriction.

mistakes.symptom: I cannot find my layer
mistakes.cause: The filter box still has text, or the layer sits in a collapsed group.
mistakes.fix: Clear the filter, or expand the group header.

mistakes.symptom: The wrong layer got edited
mistakes.cause: The previously selected layer was still active.
mistakes.fix: Click the right name first, check the card shows it, then work. Done on the layer card deselects.

protips: Alt+click on an eye is the fastest way to inspect a layer on its own.
The filter also searches group names, so typing a group name pulls up everything inside it.
Layer thumbnail size and the filter live in the same strip, so a 60-layer file stays manageable.

articles.title: What each layer is for
articles.summary: A layered template holds body paint, numbers, sponsors, tape, decals and guide layers. Knowing which is which keeps your export clean.
articles.what: A paint template (PSD) carries several kinds of layer. BODY PAINT (Car Paint) holds the livery colours. NUMBERS, SPONSORS and TAPE or stripes hold the art on top. DECALS and LOGOS (Pitbox Colors, Color Change Logos, Car_decal, Windshield Banner) hold the small stamps. TEMPLATE layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) are guides for you. They live in the group called Turn Off Before Exporting TGA.
when: You open a new template and want to know what each layer does.
You want a whole-car look on the body paint only, not on the numbers.
A number or sponsor changed colour and you need to find out why.
how: Open the layer list (right column) and read the layer names.
Hide a layer with its eye to see what it contributes.
Treat Mask and Wire as guides only. RENDER leaves them out of the car paint for you.
Put finishes on the body paint. Leave numbers, sponsors and tape as they are unless you mean to change them.
tips: Looks applied to the whole car go to the body paint layers. Numbers and sponsors stay untouched.
If you are unsure which layer holds a part, hide layers one at a time until it disappears.
pitfalls: The guide layers are not paint. RENDER leaves them out of the car paint for you.
Layer names vary by car. Judge by what the layer shows, not only by its name.

deep.heading: How the app decides a layer's role
deep.body: The app reads the layer name and its group name. The first rule that matches wins, in this order: template guide (group name with turn off, export, template or guide, or a name with mask, wire, wireframe, mandatory, template, guide, outline or uv), then numbers, sponsors, tape or stripes, body paint (car paint, body, base paint, livery, paint, base), then decals or logos (logo, decal, banner, pitbox, windshield, sticker, badge). Anything else is other art. The AI copilot uses these roles to decide what to touch.

deep.heading: A body layer with no name
deep.body: If nothing is called body, the app falls back to the bottom-most art layer that covers a big part of the sheet and treats it as the body. This rescues files whose body layer is called something like Layer 16, but a clear name is more reliable than the fallback.

deep.heading: Typical stacking order
deep.body: The ARCA test template stacks from the bottom up as: the body base layer, White Accent, Logos, Numbers, Pitbox Colors, Car_Decal, Color Change Logos, Contingency Decals, Tape, and last the guide group holding Car Mandatory, Mask and Wire. Layers higher in the list sit in front. That order is why numbers sit on top of the body paint and tape sits on top of numbers.

deep.heading: Why roles matter for finishes
deep.body: A zone that changes the body should be limited to the body paint layer, so numbers, sponsors and tape stay exactly as they are. Whole-car looks the AI applies go to the body paint layers only. Because the role comes from the name, one oddly named layer can end up classed wrongly, so rename it before you ask for a change.

faq.q: What are Pitbox Colors?
faq.a: A decal layer in many templates. The app classes it with decals and logos because its name contains pitbox.

faq.q: Can I rename layers?
faq.a: Yes, press RENAME on the layer card. Renaming changes how the app classes the layer, so use plain words such as Body Paint or Numbers.

faq.q: A layer called Body Number is numbers or body?
faq.a: Numbers. The number rule is checked before the body rule, so the first matching word decides.

faq.q: Which layers are template layers?
faq.a: Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory and anything in a group with turn off, export, template or guide in its name. They are guides, not paint.

faq.q: Why did the AI skip one of my layers?
faq.a: It may be locked or hidden, or its name put it in a different role than you expect. Unlock it or rename it.

faq.q: What if my template has no body layer?
faq.a: The app picks the bottom-most big art layer. Rename it to Body Paint so the choice is certain.

mistakes.symptom: A whole-car look repainted my sponsors
mistakes.cause: The zone covers everything instead of the body layer, or the body layer is misnamed.
mistakes.fix: Restrict the zone to the body paint layer and rename that layer clearly.

mistakes.symptom: Guide lines show up in the render
mistakes.cause: The render came from an older copy of Shokker, or the lines are drawn into the template art itself
mistakes.fix: Update Shokker: RENDER now leaves Wire, Mask and Car_Mandatory out of the car paint for you. If lines still show, hide those layers (the group Turn Off Before Exporting TGA) and render again.

mistakes.symptom: The helper treats a decal as body paint
mistakes.cause: The name contains a body word such as base or paint, which is checked before decal words.
mistakes.fix: Rename the layer so it says decal or logo.

protips: Layer names are the app's only clue to a role, so a tidy name like Numbers or Body Paint makes every later request more accurate.
If you are unsure what a layer holds, solo it with Alt+click on the eye.
Tape is checked before body words, so a layer named Tape Body is treated as tape.

articles.title: The layer card buttons
articles.summary: Select a layer and a card of buttons opens. They copy, flip, move, merge, export or delete that layer.
articles.what: Select a layer and its card opens under the layer list. The five everyday jobs are icons in one row: Duplicate Layer (Shift+click makes a copy shifted 50 px, handy for repeated sponsors), Mirror Clone (copies the layer and flips it to the opposite side of the car), Free Transform (scales and rotates it, Ctrl+T), Merge Down (joins it into the layer below, Ctrl+E) and Delete Layer. Everything else is in the More menu at the end of the row. Arrange has Solo Layer (shows only this layer; the row then says Restore Layers) and Rename. Transform has Move, Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Rotate 90° (clockwise), Pan to Layer and Fit to Layer. Effects has Stroke FX... (opens Layer Effects on the Stroke) and FX Strength. Output has Export as PNG (a transparent PNG with your Hue, Sat and Bright baked in), Make Zone from Layer, Lock Zone to Layer (Ctrl+L) and Rasterize Text. Deselect Layer is last.
when: You need the same sponsor on both sides of the car.
You want to nudge, flip or turn a logo.
You want only that layer as a PNG to send to someone.
how: Click the layer name in the list.
Pick an icon in the row, or click More at the end of the row and pick a menu row.
For a flipped copy on the other side, click Mirror Clone and then check where it landed.
Click Deselect Layer (last row of More) when finished.

actions.label: Create a zone restricted to this layer button

deep.heading: The card is two rows plus the sliders
deep.body: The card is one row of five icons and a More menu. The icons are Duplicate Layer, Mirror Clone, Free Transform, Merge Down and Delete Layer. More is grouped: Arrange (Duplicate Layer, Mirror Clone, Merge Down, Solo Layer, Rename, Delete Layer), Transform (Move, Free Transform, Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Rotate 90°, Pan to Layer, Fit to Layer), Effects (Stroke FX..., FX Strength), Output (Export as PNG, Make Zone from Layer, Lock Zone to Layer, Rasterize Text) and Deselect Layer. The Hue, Sat and Bright sliders and the opacity and blend controls sit on the same card. Old names: DUPE, MIRROR, XFORM, MERGE, DELETE, SOLO, FLIP H, FLIP V, ROT 90, EXPORT, MAKE ZONE, LOCK ZONE and DONE became the names above. A small hint at the bottom reminds you that drag or Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+] reorder layers.

deep.heading: What DUPE and MIRROR name their copies
deep.body: Duplicate Layer copies the layer in place and names the copy with the word copy added. Shift+click on Duplicate Layer offsets the copy by 50 pixels right and 50 pixels down, which is handy for rows of identical sponsors. Mirror Clone names its copy with (mirror) added, flips it and places it at the matching spot on the other side of the sheet. Both make a normal new layer that can be moved, restyled or deleted.

deep.heading: The FX multiplier button
deep.body: The effect strength button cycles in quarter steps. Each click raises the strength by 0.25 and, once it reaches 1.5 or more, wraps back to 0.25. Shift+click resets it to exactly 1.0. It scales your layer effects (stroke, glow and the like) without opening the effects panel.

deep.heading: Locks and disabled buttons
deep.body: A locked layer greys out every button that would change it: Stroke FX..., Merge Down, Flip Horizontal, Flip Vertical, Rotate 90°, Move, Free Transform and others. Solo Layer, Pan to Layer, Fit to Layer, Lock Zone to Layer and Deselect Layer still work because they do not alter pixels. Unlock the layer with the lock icon on its row when you need to edit it.

faq.q: Where did the FX and Flatten buttons go?
faq.a: FX is reachable by double-clicking the layer row, and Flatten moved once to the Actions menu because it affects the whole document.

faq.q: What is the difference between DUPE and MIRROR?
faq.a: DUPE copies the layer in place. MIRROR copies it and flips it to the opposite side of the sheet.

faq.q: Which way does ROT 90 turn?
faq.a: Clockwise, 90 degrees each press.

faq.q: What does MAKE ZONE do?
faq.a: It creates a zone limited to this layer's footprint. Give that zone a base material to style the layer.

faq.q: How do I reorder layers?
faq.a: Drag the row in the list, or use Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+] to move a layer down or up.

faq.q: Why are some buttons greyed out?
faq.a: The layer is locked. Unlock it from its row.

faq.q: Where is Flip Horizontal on the layer card now?

mistakes.symptom: DUPE seems to do nothing

mistakes.fix: Shift+click DUPE for an offset copy, or drag the new layer away.

protips: Shift+click Duplicate Layer is the quickest way to build rows of identical numbers or sponsors.
Export as PNG (More > Output) bakes in your Hue, Sat and Bright, so you can reuse a recoloured logo in another project.
Deselect Layer stops stray keys from editing the layer you just finished.

articles.title: Opacity, blend mode and colour tuning
articles.summary: Each layer has an opacity slider, a blend mode (16 of them, such as Multiply, Screen and Overlay) and Hue, Sat and Bright sliders; none damage your art. A pattern has its own separate paint mode, Overlay or Blend.
articles.what: Select a layer to see them under its row. Opacity runs 0 to 100, and you can type a number in the box beside it. The Blend dropdown offers 16 modes: Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Darken, Lighten, Color Dodge, Color Burn, Hard Light, Soft Light, Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity. Hue runs -180 to 180, Sat -100 to 100 and Bright -100 to 200. These are non-destructive, so you can set them back to 0 at any time. A Color Overlay checkbox tints the layer (start colour pink-red, 50% strength).
when: A sponsor is too loud and you want it softer.
You want a shadow layer to darken what is under it.
You want to recolour a logo without repainting it.
how: Click the layer name.
Drag Opacity, or type a % in the box.
Open the Blend dropdown and pick a mode. Use Multiply to darken and Screen to lighten.
Drag Hue, Sat or Bright to tune the colour. Set them to 0 to go back.
Tick Color Overlay to flood the layer with one colour.

tips: The AI copilot can change visibility, opacity and blend, but not delete, merge, rename or reorder.
pitfalls: A locked layer cannot be changed. Unlock it first.
Heavy blend modes can change how a finish reads on the car. Check the preview.

aliases: how to make a layer transparent

deep.heading: What each slider does
deep.body: Opacity goes from 0 to 100 percent and you can type an exact number in the box beside the slider. Press Enter to accept it or Esc to cancel your edit. Hue turns the colours around the colour wheel from -180 to 180 degrees. Sat runs from -100 to 100, where -100 removes all colour and leaves grey. Bright runs from -100 to 200, where -100 is black and 200 makes the layer three times as bright. All three are non-destructive: setting them back to 0 restores the original pixels.

deep.heading: Blend modes in plain words
deep.body: The Blend dropdown offers 16 modes: Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Darken, Lighten, Color Dodge, Color Burn, Hard Light, Soft Light, Difference, Exclusion, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity. Multiply darkens by multiplying with what is beneath, so white disappears and shadow layers sit naturally. Screen does the opposite and lightens, so black disappears. Overlay and Soft Light add contrast over what is below. Color applies only the hue and saturation of your layer, which is the safe way to recolour without losing shading.

deep.heading: Colour Overlay
deep.body: The Color Overlay checkbox floods the layer with one colour. It starts as pink-red (ff3366) at 50 percent strength with Normal blend, and you can change the colour and the amount. Because it is an effect, switching it off brings the original colours back.

deep.heading: Where the order of effects matters
deep.body: The layer is first shifted by Hue, Sat and Bright, then drawn at its opacity using its blend mode. A low opacity layer with Multiply therefore darkens less than the same layer at 100 percent. Finishes are applied on top of the composited paint, so a heavy blend mode can change how a finish reads on the car. Always check the preview.

The sliders appear on the card of the selected layer, below its row.

faq.q: Which blend mode darkens?
faq.a: Multiply. Screen lightens. Overlay and Soft Light add contrast.

faq.q: Will Hue, Sat or Bright damage my artwork?
faq.a: No. They are non-destructive. Set them back to 0 and the original comes back.

faq.q: What are the ranges?
faq.a: Opacity 0 to 100, Hue -180 to 180, Sat -100 to 100, Bright -100 to 200.

faq.q: Can the AI copilot change these?
faq.a: It can change visibility, opacity and blend mode, but not delete, merge, rename or reorder layers.

faq.q: Can I type an exact opacity?
faq.a: Yes. Type in the box beside the slider and press Enter.

faq.q: Why can I not change anything?
faq.a: The layer is locked. Unlock it from its row.

mistakes.symptom: A layer vanished after I picked a blend mode
mistakes.cause: Screen hides black and Multiply hides white, so parts of the art can drop out.
mistakes.fix: Switch back to Normal, or change the blend mode to match the art.

mistakes.symptom: The preview and my layer look different
mistakes.cause: A heavy blend mode shifts what the finish sits on.
mistakes.fix: Judge by the car preview, not the flat sheet.

mistakes.symptom: Brightness washed everything out
mistakes.cause: Bright goes up to 200 and each step is strong.
mistakes.fix: Pull it back toward 0 and add contrast with Overlay instead.

protips: Color blend mode applies only hue and saturation of the layer, so it recolours without flattening shading.
Hue and Sat are applied before the layer is drawn, so you can tint a flat logo without touching the layer itself.
Esc in the opacity box cancels the typed number and keeps the previous value.

articles.title: Layer Effects
articles.summary: Layer Effects adds a drop shadow, glow, stroke, colour overlay or bevel to a layer without changing the art itself.
articles.what: Open it from Stroke FX... in the More menu of the layer card (Effects group). Each effect has an on or off box and its own sliders. Drop Shadow: opacity 0 to 100 (starts at 75), angle 0 to 360 (135), distance 0 to 50 (5), size 0 to 50 (5). Outer Glow: opacity 0 to 100 (80), size 1 to 50 (10), spread 0 to 100 (0). Stroke: width 1 to 20 (2), opacity 0 to 100 (100) and a position dropdown. Color Overlay: opacity 0 to 100 (50). Bevel: a direction dropdown, depth 1 to 10 (3), size 1 to 20 (5) and soften 0 to 10 (0). Clear All removes every effect. Apply keeps them. Cancel closes without keeping changes.
when: A number or logo needs an outline so it reads on a busy paint.
You want a soft shadow under a sponsor.
You want a bevelled look on lettering.
how: Select the layer and open More on its card and choose Stroke FX... under Effects.
Tick the effect you want.
Set its colour, then drag the sliders and watch the live preview.
Click Apply to keep it, or Cancel to drop it.

deep.heading: Starting colours and defaults
deep.body: Each effect starts switched off with a ready colour. Drop Shadow is black at 75 percent, angle 135, distance 5 and size 5. Outer Glow is cyan at 80 percent with size 10 and spread 0. Stroke is white, 2 px wide, 100 percent, positioned Outside. Color Overlay is pink-red at 50 percent. Bevel is Up (Raised) with depth 3, size 5 and soften 0. Ticking an effect box turns it on with these numbers, so you only change what you need.

deep.heading: Order they are drawn in
deep.body: The app draws them in a fixed order: Drop Shadow, then Outer Glow, then Stroke, then Color Overlay, then Bevel last. You cannot reorder them, so choose colours with that order in mind.

deep.heading: Stroke position
deep.body: The Position dropdown offers Outside, Center and Inside. Outside adds a ring around the art and makes the letter look slightly bolder without moving the original edge. Inside keeps the ring within the original shape, so the art stays the same size. Center straddles the edge. For small numbers Outside with a contrasting colour at 2 to 4 px is the safest choice.

deep.heading: Live preview and what is kept
deep.body: While the dialog is open the canvas shows a live preview. Apply keeps the effects, Cancel (or Esc) discards changes made in this session, and Clear All removes every effect from the layer. Opening and closing the dialog without changing anything adds nothing to your undo history. Effects never change the layer's own pixels.

faq.q: Can I stack several effects?
faq.a: Yes, each effect has its own box and you can tick all five.

faq.q: Do effects damage the artwork?
faq.a: No. They are non-destructive. Clear All brings back the plain layer.

faq.q: What are the stroke positions?
faq.a: Outside, Center and Inside.

faq.q: What are the bevel directions?
faq.a: Up (Raised) and Down (Sunken).

faq.q: How do I cancel my changes?
faq.a: Press Cancel or Esc. Clear All is different: it removes every effect on the layer.

faq.q: Why is STROKE FX greyed out?
faq.a: The layer is locked, and the dialog shows a lock notice. Unlock it from its row.

faq.q: Can Outer Glow actually light up the track around my number?
faq.a: Outer Glow draws a blurred coloured halo from the layer image and composites it into the picture. Its reviewed Canvas2D path creates painted pixels, not a light source that illuminates the track. Inspect readable detail in simulator lighting; a visible halo is not emission.

articles.title: Merge, flatten and blank layers
articles.summary: Merge Down and Merge Visible have different identity and Zone-link behavior. Preserved IDs do not preserve separate artwork footprints. Flatten discards the old layer list; inspect singular and multi-layer restrictions explicitly.
articles.what: MERGE down on a layer card joins it into the layer below. Ctrl+click several names and the merge button shows the count and joins them. In the Actions menu, Merge visible (Ctrl+Shift+E) joins all visible layers into one while hidden layers survive. Flatten document puts the whole document into one layer. It first lists hidden layers and zone links that would be lost. + Blank layer adds a clear layer for the Retouch brushes.
when: The layer list is long and you want to tidy it.
You need a clear layer to paint on without touching the art.
You are done editing and want one flat layer.
how: Select the upper layer and use MERGE down (Ctrl+E in LAYER mode) to combine it with the layer below. Read any lock, hidden-layer or group-boundary warning.
For several chosen layers, Ctrl+click their names and use the merge button showing the count. For all visible artwork, use Actions > Merge visible (Ctrl+Shift+E); hidden layers remain.
Inspect the resulting combined artwork and Zone restrictions. A combined layer cannot independently identify numbers and sponsors that now share its pixels.

Flatten is a separate operation that discards the old layer list and clears layer links. Keep the original source and a saved project; review the warning and use the applicable Undo if a merge changes the wrong artwork.

deep.heading: MERGE down has four conditions
deep.body: MERGE down joins a layer into the one below it, and it refuses with a message unless four things are true: there is a layer below, the upper layer is visible, neither layer is locked, and both sit in the same PSD group. If you try it across a group boundary the app stops and suggests merging inside one group or flattening. The result keeps the lower layer's place and name.

deep.heading: Blank layers
deep.body: + Blank layer adds an empty, fully transparent layer covering the whole sheet at 100 percent opacity with Normal blend, and selects it for you. It goes on top and is the target for the Color Brush and other retouch tools. It also arrives from the shortcut Ctrl+Shift+N.

deep.heading: ID restriction versus actual artwork footprint
deep.body: Merge Down migrates sourceLayer and deduplicated sourceLayers to the surviving lower layer. That layer now contains combined artwork, so the Zone can cover more pixels than before. Merge Visible only migrates singular sourceLayer in the inspected handler; Flatten clears singular fields but leaves plural arrays. Check the actual Zone target after either operation.

faq.q: Why does MERGE down say no layer below?
faq.a: The selected layer is the bottom one. Choose a layer that has another layer under it.

faq.q: Why will it not merge?
faq.a: A locked layer, a hidden upper layer, or a PSD group boundary. The message tells you which.

faq.q: Does Merge visible delete my hidden layers?
faq.a: No, they survive. Flatten does discard them.

faq.q: What happens to my zone restrictions when I merge?
faq.a: It depends on the operation. Merge Down moves an upper-layer link to the surviving lower layer. Merge Visible migrates participating visible-layer links to its surviving base. Flatten clears the old layer links. Inspect singular and multi-layer restrictions and the combined artwork footprint; preserved IDs do not keep separate number/sponsor targets.

faq.q: Can I undo a merge?
faq.a: Yes, press Ctrl+Z straight away. After many steps, the layer undo list is limited, so save a project first.

faq.q: Where is the keyboard shortcut?
faq.a: Ctrl+E merges down, Ctrl+Shift+E merges visible and Ctrl+Shift+N adds a blank layer. They work in LAYER mode.

faq.q: My numbers and sponsor are merged into the paint layer. How do I give only numbers a satin surface?
faq.a: A merged layer restriction includes the artwork that shares that layer, so it cannot identify only numbers. Use a checked local selection or mask around the intended number artwork, or recover/separate the original artwork first. Choose its material separately from its paint colour; Use source paint does not itself isolate the target.

faq.q: Does merging artwork keep separate material targets for numbers and sponsors?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Inspect the resulting layer contents and zone coverage. A restriction to a combined layer may include both elements. Use separate artwork or checked local masks when they need different materials.

Hide what you want to keep apart before Merge visible. Only the visible layers merge.

articles.title: Open a layered template

articles.what: Click Open Layered on the layer list, or Open Paint... > Layered template next to Source Paint. Pick the template for the same car you drive. The layer tree appears in the layer list with the guide layers inside their group. Use Actions > Place image... to add a single PNG, JPG, WebP or GIF as a new layer on top (+ Layer adds a blank layer).

Inspect the imported layers and the source appearance before editing. Preserve the original file; a displayed composite does not prove all layers imported as editable pixels.

deep.heading: Which files work
deep.body: The file picker for Open Layered is titled Open Layered File and only offers .psd (Photoshop), .xcf (GIMP) and .ora (GIMP and Krita) files. A TGA, PNG or JPEG opens as a flat paint with no layers, through Source Paint. Use the template for the car you drive at its normal 2048 by 2048 size. A big PSD can take up to a minute to open, and the RENDER button wakes up when the file has finished loading.

deep.heading: What the importer tells you it skipped
deep.body: After a layered open the app can show a short note. If a layer uses a blend mode that is not supported here, it is imported as Normal and the note lists up to four names. If a layer is not made of pixels, such as a live text layer or an adjustment layer, it cannot be imported, and the note lists up to four names so you know what is missing. The picture of the whole document is also read from the file and must match its size, otherwise the open stops with an error instead of showing a wrong car.

deep.heading: Your layers come back after a crash
deep.body: If the app closed unexpectedly while you were working on the same file, reopening it asks whether to restore your work. The message starts "SPB found your work from an interrupted session" and lists what comes back: layers you added (including live text), layers you painted on, layer masks and adjustment layers, with their order, visibility and opacity. If you say yes, Ctrl+Z undoes the restore in one step. A layer that had not been saved yet comes back empty. A flat image (TGA, PNG or JPEG) works too: the layers you added on top of it come back when you reopen that same file. It does not replace a saved project, so save one when you finish a stretch of work. If the file is a different one, the old work is not offered.

deep.heading: Opening starts a fresh edit history
deep.body: Opening a new layered file clears the source-pixel undo history, and zone links to layers are re-pointed at the incoming layers. Treat the open as a new starting point. Save your current project first if you want to return to it.

faq.q: Which file types does Open Layered accept?
faq.a: PSD from Photoshop, XCF from GIMP and ORA from GIMP or Krita.

faq.q: Why are there no layers after I opened my paint?
faq.a: A TGA, PNG or JPEG is flat. Open the layered template to get layers.

faq.q: How long should a PSD take?
faq.a: Wait for the import completion note and populated layer list rather than treating elapsed time or an enabled RENDER button as proof of full editable fidelity. The note reports layers loaded, diagnostics, or a source-composite fallback. A failed import reports an error and retains the previous source.

faq.q: My text layers are missing.
faq.a: The importer drops entries reported as having no pixels, and the note names non-pixel layers it could not import. It does not reconstruct editable text from those entries. Preserve the original, rasterize the missing content in your editor if needed, then inspect the import again.

faq.q: My blend modes look different.
faq.a: Unsupported leaf blend modes are normalized to Normal and listed in a note. Unsupported group semantics or a critical composite mismatch can trigger a source-composite fallback, so check the completion warning and actual imported appearance before assuming every layer remains independently editable.

faq.q: Can I use any car's template?
faq.a: Use the one for the car you drive. Another car has different panels and will not line up.

articles.title: Guide layers: grouping and export checks
articles.summary: Export excludes imported pixels grouped under Turn Off Before Export only when the guide filter is active and safe recomposition succeeds. Bare layer names do not qualify; flat baked lines cannot be removed that way. Inspect layer paths and actual output, and retain real mandatory artwork.
articles.what: The active render guide filter recognizes imported layers through groupName/path/groupChain entries matching Turn Off Before Export, not by a bare Wire, Mask or Car_Mandatory name alone. It needs a loaded layer tree, pixels and an active guide-filter path. A disabled filter or failed safe recomposition can return the ordinary live composite. Lines baked into a flat image are not removable guide layers. Inspect actual layer contents, source/output and the reported exclusions; do not blindly hide a mandatory artwork layer or guarantee that Render removes every guide.
when: Your car in iRacing shows green lines or panel outlines.
You want to judge a look without outlines in the preview.
You hid the guides and need them back for editing.
how: Compare the original SOURCE with the current output. Determine whether the lines are separate imported layers or already baked into flat paint pixels.

Inspect the actual guide group/path and individual layer contributions. The render filter recognizes the Turn Off Before Export grouping, not a universal list of layer names. Preserve real mandatory artwork.

For a clean visual inspection, select only the intended guide layer before toggling its eye; a multi-selection can toggle all selected layers. A Source/Preview view button is not an export-content switch.

Review the actual render result, exclusion message and current file. A fallback composite or unrecognized group may keep lines. A flat image with baked lines needs a clean source or a deliberate artwork correction; rerendering alone does not remove them.

faq.q: Why do I have two numbers on my car?
faq.a: Check separately for an old baked-in number, additional Number Kit layers, and an iRacing stamp over your artwork. Recognized imported guide-group exclusion is not a guarantee that all number graphics were removed.

faq.q: Which layers are the guides?
faq.a: Inspect their actual contents and imported group/path. The current render filter uses the Turn Off Before Export group ancestry; a bare Wire/Mask/Car_Mandatory name is not sufficient for that filter.

faq.q: Do I need to turn them off every time?
faq.a: Recognized imported guide-group layers can be excluded by the active render path, but loaded pixels, grouping, flags and successful recomposition matter. Inspect the real output rather than assume every named guide disappears.

faq.q: Why is the wireframe in my paint?
faq.a: Check whether it is baked into a flat source, belongs to an unrecognized imported group, or survived a disabled/failed guide-free composition. Inspect actual layer content and output; do not discard mandatory art based on its name.

faq.q: Can the helper do this for me?
faq.a: Yes. Type hide the template layers and Undo brings them back.

faq.q: Why did a zone stop painting after I hid the group?
faq.a: A zone restricted to a layer in a hidden group paints nothing. Choose a visible layer for it.

faq.q: Does the preview view button change my export?
faq.a: No. Template view buttons only change what you see, not what is rendered.

faq.q: Is it normal to see the wire outline on the car after a render?
faq.a: Inspect the actual output file and source. The guide filter can exclude recognized imported guide groups; it cannot identify or erase lines baked into a flat image, and its fallback can use the live composite.

faq.q: What does Guide layers left out of the render mean?
faq.a: The active render path successfully recomposited without the recognized imported guide-group layers and reported their names. It does not certify every possible guide or remove baked flat-image lines.

deep.heading: How the Mask is read
deep.body: On the template Mask layer, clear pixels are paintable panels and solid pixels are dead space. The app reads it that way and accepts it only when the paintable share is between 8 percent and 92 percent of the sheet. If less than 12 percent of the Mask is solid, the app assumes it was drawn the other way round and flips it.

deep.heading: Mask plus Wire gives you separate panels
deep.body: The Wire layer draws a green outline around every panel. The app thickens those outlines by one small block, removes them from the paintable area, and counts each remaining clear piece as one panel. That is how it tells the hood, roof and sides apart. If a dense Wire mesh would shatter the panels, so that the split keeps under 70 percent of the paintable area, it separates panels by trimming thin bridges instead.

deep.heading: No Mask layer on the sheet
deep.body: A flat paint file with no Mask can still work. If the sheet still shows the template dead-space tone, or transparency, everything else counts as paintable. If it shows neither, the app falls back to the footprint of the body paint layers, which only splits panels that have empty space between them.

deep.heading: What it changes in practice
deep.body: Shokker AI looks that cover the whole car, and an Everything zone made by the copilot, use the paintable area as their region, so dead space is left alone. The app also stores a coarse 32 by 32 fingerprint of the paintable area to recognise the same car template again. Mask and Wire are guide layers, so they are ignored when the app works out which zone owns which paint.

deep.heading: Three guides, three jobs
deep.body: Wire draws each panel outline in bright green, and the lines between them in the mesh are white or grey. Mask is the paintable map: clear is panel, solid is dead space. deep.heading: How the app finds them
deep.body: The app treats a layer as a template guide when its own name, or the name of its group, contains words such as mask, wire, wireframe, mandatory, template, guide, outline or export. deep.heading: Why the AI copilot wants Wire and Mask

deep.heading: How zones treat them

deep.heading: Why it exists
deep.body: Sim-stamped numbers and sponsors take on the spec map underneath them. Over chrome, candy or metallic bodywork a white number can turn into a mirror and become unreadable. Decal Rescue sets a safe, non-metallic spec under the stamp footprint and leaves the paint colours alone. Open it from MASK > Advanced spec utilities, then Decal Rescue Kit.

deep.heading: The three presets in numbers
deep.body: Flat Vinyl is metal 0, roughness 100, clearcoat 110. Satin Decal is metal 0, roughness 100, clearcoat 75. Gloss Decal is metal 0, roughness 42, clearcoat 22. The spec alpha is set to 255. On the clearcoat channel 16 is maximum gloss and 255 is dull, so 22 is almost full gloss, 75 is a soft sheen and 110 is flat.

deep.heading: What it does to the zone
deep.body: It works on the active zone only and needs a selection in it. It sets the zone base to a flat Foundation material, keeps the source paint colours, and clears every pattern, overlay and extra base on that zone. It also clears any layer restriction so the exact footprint you drew is what reaches the spec. One Undo restores the zone's previous recipe.

deep.heading: What stops it
deep.body: With no selection in the active zone you get a message to draw the number or sponsor footprint first. If the zone has its Base, Pattern or Intensity locked, you must unlock them first. If the zone has a layer restriction, the kit shows a note that Rescue will clear it.

articles.title: Race Wear Studio: a worn-car look in one click
articles.summary: Race Wear Studio (Car > Race Wear...) puts a removable worn-car layer on the car in one click, in five looks from Showroom to Endurance 24 h. It changes paint and spec together, undoes exactly and is saved with the project.
articles.what: Race Wear Studio is a small window with five looks: Showroom, Short-Track Oval, Road Course, Dirt Late Model and Endurance 24 h. Pick one and the car gets that kind of racing wear straight away: dirt and spray rise behind the wheels, bugs and stone chips hit the nose and leading edges, rubber sits at door height. An overlay on the sheet shows where it landed. The wear is one layer you can hide or remove. It is not painted into your artwork. Paint and spec change together when you render: mud is matte, rubber has no clear coat, bare-metal chips are metallic and dulled clear loses its gloss. The wear fades softly towards panel edges and holes in the template.
when: You want Race Wear Studio to make the whole car look raced in one click.
You want Race Wear Studio’s worn look on a layer you can switch off or remove.
You want paint wear and spec wear to match without painting both.
how: 1. Open the Car menu in the tool band and choose Race Wear... (it is in the Across The Car group, after Car-Space Fade).
2. Pick a look: Showroom, Short-Track Oval, Road Course, Dirt Late Model or Endurance 24 h. The car is worn straight away.
3. Set Laps (it says hours for Endurance) to build the wear up or down. Strength fades the whole layer in or out. New Seed gives a different pattern of the same look.
4. Keep decals clean keeps numbers and sponsor decals free of wear. Mask Off Selection keeps the wear off whatever is selected, and Clear Mask takes that mask away.
5. Hide takes the layer off without losing it. Remove deletes it. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo every change exactly. Done closes the window.
6. Render as usual. Check the gloss with the Shine Lens first if you like.
7. Save Project keeps the layer with its mask and strength, and opening the project brings it back.

articles.title: Does opacity fade the shine, or only the colour?
articles.summary: Layer opacity fades only the colour: the shine (spec) under a layer stays what its zone gives, unless the layer has its own Layer Material, whose shine does fade with the layer. To fade the shine too, lower the zone SPEC STRENGTH, give the layer a Layer Material, or use Car-Space Fade.
articles.what: Opacity is a paint control. The shine of the car lives in a second map (the spec file), and most opacity sliders only touch the colour map, so the answer depends on which opacity you mean. Layer opacity (the slider under a layer in the Layers panel) fades that layer into what is below it, in colour only. The shine under that spot is whatever the zone there gives it, so a half-faded sponsor over a chrome zone still sits on chrome. The one exception is a layer that has a Layer Material (Material / Spec menu, Whole Car, Layer Materials...): its shine follows the layer exactly, so at 50 percent opacity its material is mixed half and half with what is under it, and a hidden layer has no shine at all. Pattern Opacity (the PATTERN section of a zone) fades the pattern in the paint only. The shine a pattern adds comes from its own Spec amount slider, which starts at 0 and is independent of paint Opacity and Strength; the base finish keeps its own shine. A zone has no opacity slider. BASE STRENGTH mixes its paint back toward your original colours and leaves the shine alone, while SPEC STRENGTH weakens the material itself (metal, roughness and clearcoat move toward neutral) and leaves the colour alone. Lower both to fade both. The Opacity slider in the selection bar next to Zoom only sets how strongly the zone overlay shows on screen; it changes neither colour nor shine in your render.
when: You lowered a layer or zone opacity and the shine did not fade.
You want to know whether opacity changes the spec or only the colour.
You want the colour and the shine to fade together.
how: 1. Faded layer still looks glossy or chrome in the sim? That is normal: its shine comes from the zone under it. Select the layer, open Material / Spec > Whole Car > Layer Materials... and give it a material. From then on its shine follows the layer opacity.
2. Zone: lower BASE STRENGTH to fade the paint toward your original colours and SPEC STRENGTH to fade the shine. Lower both to fade both.
3. Pattern: Opacity fades the pattern colour only. The shine a pattern adds comes from its own Spec amount slider (it starts at 0), which does not change with paint Opacity or Strength.
4. Along the car: Car > Car-Space Fade... fades colour and shine together, nose to tail or bottom to top.
5. By hand: the Material Brush honours Opacity, so a 50 percent chrome stroke renders as half chrome. The Spec Brush paints only the shine.
6. Check it with the Shine Lens or the Live Preview, then RENDER and press Ctrl+R in iRacing.
tips: The Opacity slider in the selection bar never changes your paint or your shine: it is a screen aid for the zone overlay.
A hidden layer has no Layer Material shine at all, so hiding one is a clean way to test what a layer was adding.
pitfalls: A zone that picks pixels by colour follows the colour: fade the colour enough and some pixels can fall out of that zone, and the zone shine leaves with them.
Lowering BASE STRENGTH alone leaves the full shine on a faded colour, which can look like a glossy ghost.

deep.heading: Why a faded layer can still look shiny

faq.a: The inspected PNG handler requires a matching layer and image, but has no visibility or lock refusal. Hidden or locked artwork can be exported by this path. Exporting it is distinct from showing, painting or compositing it into the car.

faq.q: Why is the downloaded layer PNG name changed or shortened?
faq.a: The handler replaces characters outside letters, digits, spaces, underscores and hyphens with underscores, truncates the base name to 60 characters and appends .png. Different long or punctuated names may produce similar download names; check actual files to avoid mixing up artwork.

faq.q: Does a successful layer Export return prove the PNG was saved in my chosen folder?
faq.a: The handler creates a PNG data URL, sets an anchor download name and clicks it. Returning true confirms that request path completed, not a read-back of a disk file or a chosen-folder write. Check the browser/app download result and file before relying on the export.

faq.q: What should I check when a single-layer PNG export fails or says no pixels?
faq.a: The handler returns false if the ID has no matching image, and catches errors during canvas/data-URL export. Check the actual layer and loaded image, then the failure message. This is separate from a full paint/spec render and does not justify deleting your project or source artwork.
